info.description:
The HTTP API behind Tearleads clients. Document and key material is
end-to-end encrypted, so request bodies carry ciphertext, signed manifests,
and key envelopes that only the client SDK can produce or open.

This document is generated from the Zod operation registry in
`@tearleads/validators`, which remains the runtime authority. Rules that
JSON Schema cannot express are listed per operation under
`x-tearleads-runtime-refinements`. See the protocol specification for
message semantics, proofs, and failure handling.
info.title: Tearleads Protocol API

get.description: Returns `ok` when the API process is serving requests; load balancers and clients use it as a liveness probe. It needs no session, and a request that carries a body is refused with 413.

post.description: Starts sign-in for a registered identity: the server stores a short-lived random challenge for the signing key fingerprint, and the client signs it and sends the signature to `POST /auth/verify`. No session is needed; an unknown fingerprint returns 404.
Ends the session that made the request, so its bearer token stops working. Any signed-in user may call it.

post.summary: Register an identity and bootstrap its root state
post.description: Creates a new identity from its signing and encapsulation public keys and, in one transaction, provisions its personal organization: the reserved `Admins` and `Members` groups, the root container, and their signed policies and metadata documents. The response carries a fresh login challenge, so the client signs in next with `POST /auth/verify`. A signing key that is already registered returns 409.

put.description: Uploads one part's encrypted bytes through the API, for object stores that cannot sign direct upload URLs. Only the stage's owner may call it, and stores that do sign URLs reject this route. The part's declared byte length and SHA-256 headers must match the bytes sent.

post.summary: Authorize a direct multipart blob part upload
post.description: Returns a short-lived signed URL for uploading one part of a blob stage directly to object storage, for parts after the first batch or to renew an expired URL. Only the stage's owner may call it. The URL is scoped to the exact part number, byte length, and Content-MD5, and expiry never invalidates parts already uploaded.

get.description: Returns a blob stage's status so a client can resume an interrupted upload. Only the exact 404 `multipart_blob_stage_not_found` or 409 `multipart_blob_stage_expired` responses prove the stage is gone and permit starting a fresh one; any other failure means the client should keep its resumable state.

post.description: Opens a blob stage for an encrypted upload, declaring the final byte length, SHA-256 digest, and organization, and returns upload sources for the first parts so they can start at once. The caller must belong to the organization. The stage expires after one hour; nothing becomes readable until an attachment bind promotes it.

Removes an active attachment binding from its document slot through a signed `attachment.detach` event. Requires write access through an authorizing container path. A blob left with no active binding is kept for the attachment-retention grace period before garbage collection.

post.summary: Bind or replace a blob attachment
post.description: Attaches an encrypted blob to an attachment slot in a document, or replaces the slot's current binding, through a signed `attachment.bind` event. When it names a blob stage, the server assembles and verifies the staged upload and promotes it to committed blob storage; this is the only way to complete an upload. Requires write access through an authorizing container path; a stale binding or path head returns 409, and an organization without active billing returns 402.

The request must be signed by the caller within the last ten minutes and cite a stored `Members` group head the caller has belonged to ever since. A personal organization, or a caller who is its only administrator, is refused.
